I just bought a new headphone and I need a few song/music suggestions to test (in all aspects) my headphones. I always end up playing the first song in my playlist to test it.

EDIT : Thank you all for your suggestions..!! These are some nice songs you people have suggested. I'm sure it helped others too.
What songs/music do you use to test your just bought headphones?

Newer Pink Floyd music (The Division Bell) is often used, as it is known for being well mastered, and have some musical complexity.

I do, however, tend to go through a handful of songs from different genres that I often listen to, to make sure it sounds nice with what I'll actually use it for. If it sounds good with the first two songs off King Crimson's 'In the Court of the Crimson King', it usually works for me.

Just don't go for the remastered versions, they tend to have been ran through comprehensive compressors, distorting the sound quality and removing dynamics!

If you don't have to turn up the volume when listening to Pink Floyd, it's "always" a compressed remaster.
It's why you use the original vinyls ;)

Ain't nobody got time for that!

Seriously though, I find the vinyl format to be quite tedious in usage. I much prefer buying CD's, ripping them in a lossless format, and stream them digitally to a DAC. But a lot of people appreciate the tactile vinyl feel, and I can obviously see why! It's almost like a book vs. e-book.
I'm not hating on CDs. I got plenty hahaha! Vinyls just.. I dunno. I think it's the size of the album artwork that really does it for me, which sounds really petty, but I dunno.

I worked at an audio shop for a while, selling vinyl amongst other things. I think you hit the nail on the head with the artwork, people like to play the vinyl and kick back with a beer while flipping through the large cover and immersing themselves completely in the sort of expanded atmosphere that gives you.
King Crimson is great for that. I always test new equipment with Starless... at least that, or Jethro Tull's Locomotive Breath.
Revolution 9 by the Beatles. Gives a wide range of noises and sounds, and lots of left-right speaker usage. Works a charm.
Finally, some sort of reason for that song to exist. It does sound kind of like a sound check on acid.

Simple Math - Manchester Orchestra

The production value is very good, and it is mixed very well.

Grum - The Really Long One

Good song, lots of variation in terms of pitch (both high and low), and of course to listen to the awesome part at around 4:12 :D

Global Communication - 14:31

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vv091qdGzjU

Useful things about that song:

  • Good dynamic range.
  • The grandfather clock ticking allows you to feel how realistically the headphones reproduce "natural" sounds: Can you imagine the clock standing in front of you?
  • A lot of frequency sweeps in all pitch ranges.
  • Repetitive, allows you to listen to the same sounds multiple times without rewinding.

Bohemian Rhapsody. The shift in style and tone really let you know if there will be any issues with a variety of audio, from audio books (soft spoken opening) to distortion in the heavier, frenetic parts.

I typically use Agalloch. My go to is to just turn on "Marrow of the Spirit" simply because the first two tracks have so many different types of sound. Rage Against The Machine's debut album is often cited as the perfectly produced album, and used to test speakers/headphones. Not sure how true this is though. When it comes to burning in new speakers, you want to play a broad range of frequencies at a high volume, so something like pink noise is perfect. There are lots of useful videos on Youtube for this type of thing https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L3CiZxstvEA
Porter Robinson Worlds album. It's a treat all on its on, but with new cans? It's a roller coaster from start to finish.

Uptown Funk. It's not that I love the song. It just has a very wide range of mid low and high. It also has a pop-rap bass line, as well as more jazzy horn segments and a passable guitar sample. Sets a pretty good baseline for how the headphones could handle a lot of different genres
